title: 5-6. THE BEST PART OF THE LAND

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Pharaoh said to Joseph, 'Your father and your brothers have come to you, and the land of Egypt is before you; settle your father and your brothers in the best part of the land. Let them live in Goshen. And if you know of any among them with special ability, put them in charge of my own livestock.'" — Gen 47:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh gives more than was asked. The brothers requested permission to stay in Goshen. Pharaoh grants Goshen and calls it the best part of the land — and then offers employment to any of them with ability.

Why such generosity to a family of foreign shepherds? Because of Joseph. The favour flows entirely through him. Pharaoh is not repaying the brothers for anything; he is honouring the man who saved his kingdom.

That is how we come to God. Every good thing we receive comes to us through Another. We are not rewarded for our record — we are welcomed on Christ's account. God is able to give freely to people like us because of what His Son has done, and He gives generously (Rom 8:32).

But hold the tension honestly. The best part of Egypt was a real gift, and it was also the place their descendants would one day be enslaved. God's kindness here is genuine, but it does not guarantee that Egypt will always be kind. Blessings received in this world are real and worth thanking God for. They are simply not the final thing.

Receive what God gives with open hands and a grateful heart, and keep your hope fixed on what cannot be taken.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has God given you more than you asked for?
2. Do you find it easy to accept that your welcome rests on Christ, not on your record?
3. What good gift are you holding too tightly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for giving generously through Your Son and not according to what I deserve. Help me receive Your gifts gratefully while keeping my hope in what lasts. Amen.
